summary: sextant-cli-darwin-amd64 ships a WebSocket-driven remote PTY backdoor with Anthropic API key theft
details: The darwin/amd64 Go binary shipped in this package (bin/sxt) links github.com/creack/pty and github.com/coder/websocket and contains the hardcoded endpoints wss://relay.sextant.top and https://relay.sextant.top/install. The binary connects out to relay.sextant.top over WebSocket and wires the remote stream to a local pseudo-terminal, giving the operator of relay.sextant.top an interactive shell on the installer's host (full-host RCE / persistent backdoor). The same binary embeds the regex sk-ant-[a-z0-9]+-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,} (Anthropic API key format) together with the strings CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=, https://api.anthropic.com/v1/models, https://claude.ai/install.sh, and a reference to google/gemini-cli, targeting the installer's Claude and Gemini CLI configuration and API keys for extraction over the same relay channel. The binary also performs host geolocation reconnaissance via http://ip-api.com/json/?fields=status,message,country,countryCode,city,timezone,query, fingerprinting the installer's public IP, city, country, and timezone. Package metadata contradicts the advertised purpose: the license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, self-labeling the package as a Claude-control tool by author 'ddos798' while presenting to installers as a Sextant CLI platform binary.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
